title: Extend a Guardrail — Why Some Families Refuse You
note: Six families in this vocabulary are sealed: safety, injection, consent, disclosure, the delegation-chain family, and the human-loop routing terminal. They are sealed because for these the ordinary tighten-only guarantee is not enough. Everywhere else, the worst a contributor can do is make the vocabulary stricter — but a sealed family is one where even ADDING a label could open a gap, because a new label is a new bucket an act can be sorted into, and a bucket that is not the refusal bucket is a permission. Sealing is refusal of the whole contribution surface, not a direction restriction: an overlay that only tightens is refused too, because the point is that these definitions are not negotiable by the parties relying on them. HONEST SCOPE, and it matters: the seal here is AUTHORED INTENT. Whether a given runtime enforces it is a property of that runtime's fold, not of these bytes — a consumer that wants the guarantee must verify its own engine refuses overlays against sealed specs rather than assuming the declaration is self-enforcing.
